\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{booktabs}

\title{Yield Response of Winter Wheat to Delayed Sowing
on Clay Soils: Third Year Report}
\author{Field Crops Station, Easton}
\date{March 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Delayed sowing is the principal adaptation available to winter
wheat growers on heavy clay soils when autumn rainfall prevents
timely drilling.
This third year report summarises variety trial results from the
2023--2025 harvest cycles, comparing four commercial varieties
under standard and delayed sowing dates.
Mean yield penalties for delayed sowing ranged from 1.3 to 1.6
t/ha across varieties, while grain protein rose by 0.5 to 0.6
percentage points.
The station recommends retaining the current variety list and
treating the protein premium as partial compensation for the
yield penalty.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Autumn rainfall in the district has exceeded the thirty-year
mean in seven of the last ten seasons, and the window for
timely drilling on the station's clay soils has narrowed
accordingly.
Growers facing a saturated seedbed must choose between drilling
into poor conditions and delaying sowing until the soil can
carry machinery again.
The agronomic consequences of the second choice are well
documented for light land but poorly quantified for the heavy
clays that dominate this district.
The station's variety trial, now in its third year, was
designed to close that gap.

\section{Materials and Methods}
Four commercial winter wheat varieties were sown in a
randomised block design with four replicates.
Each variety was drilled at two sowing dates: a standard date
in the first week of October and a delayed date between three
and five weeks later, as soil conditions allowed.
Plots were combine-harvested and yields corrected to fifteen
percent moisture.
Grain protein was determined by near-infrared spectroscopy on
cleaned samples.

\section{Results}
Mean grain yields and protein contents for the three harvest
cycles are summarised in Table~\ref{tab:yield}.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{Grain yield and grain protein of four winter wheat
varieties under standard and delayed sowing, 2023--2025 means.}
\label{tab:yield}
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
Variety & Sowing & Grain yield (t/ha) & Grain protein (\%) \\
\midrule
Avalon & Standard & 8.4 & 11.2 \\
Avalon & Delayed & 7.1 & 11.8 \\
Bastion & Standard & 8.9 & 10.8 \\
Bastion & Delayed & 7.6 & 11.4 \\
Crispin & Standard & 8.1 & 11.6 \\
Crispin & Delayed & 6.8 & 12.1 \\
Dynast & Standard & 9.2 & 10.5 \\
Dynast & Delayed & 7.9 & 11.0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Every variety lost yield under delayed sowing, and the ranking
of varieties was the same at both sowing dates.
The yield penalty was smallest for Crispin and largest for
Dynast, although Dynast remained the highest yielding variety
under both regimes.
Grain protein rose under delayed sowing in every case, the
increase tracking the yield penalty rather than the variety.

\section{Discussion}
The consistency of the variety ranking across sowing dates
simplifies advice: growers on clay soils need not hold a
separate variety in reserve for late drilling.
The protein premium under delayed sowing partly offsets the
yield penalty wherever milling contracts pay for protein, and
in two of the three trial years the premium covered roughly
half the value of the lost grain.
Trial results cannot say whether earlier lifting of soil
compaction by cover crops would widen the drilling window;
a separate trial addressing that question enters its first
year this autumn.

\section{Conclusion}
Delayed sowing on the district's clay soils cost between 1.3
and 1.6 t/ha across the four varieties tested, with a partial
compensation in grain protein.
The current variety list remains fit for purpose under both
sowing regimes, and the station's recommendation is unchanged.
Growers are advised to treat the delayed-sowing penalty as a
planning figure rather than a worst case, since the trial's
delayed dates were moderate by the standards of the wettest
recent autumns.
\end{document}
